Read a programming template (PV) from a docx file

Source: R/read_pv.R
read_pv.Rd

Reads the item table(s) of one or more PVs (Programmiervorlagen) in docx format and splits every item into its tags (--va:, --vb:, --we:, --ef: etc.). The result is the basis for label_test() and value_label_test(), but can also be used directly, e.g. to look up the ef-tag of an item.

Usage

read_pv(path)

Arguments

path

Path to a PV in docx format. Can also be a character vector of several paths, the PVs are then combined.

Value

A data frame with one row per item and the columns pv (file name), item (text of the first table column, usually the item number), one column per tag (named after the tag, e.g. va, vb, we; NA if the item has no such tag) and text (the full text of the item).

Details

Every table row that contains at least one tag becomes one row of the result. The text of a tag runs from its tag line to the next tag line or to --end--. Tags that occur more than once in an item are joined with a line break. Lines before the first tag are ignored. Non-breaking spaces are turned into normal spaces and trailing blanks are removed, otherwise the text is kept as it is in the PV (including markers like [ZS] or [MF]).

See also

label_test() and value_label_test(), which compare the data with the PV.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
pv <- read_pv("NEPS_B180_SC6_EP_26ET_V2_2_20250312.docx")
pv[, c("item", "va", "vb")]

# several PVs at once
pv <- read_pv(c("PV_26ET.docx", "PV_27AL.docx"))
} # }
